transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Sam Lee (Skyline - Head of ML), Jordan Kim (Skyline - Eng Manager)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Skyline is evaluating Redwood's PLG quickstart path vs dedicated/private for a customer-facing recommender. Key concerns: time-to-first-token, free credits for evaluation, latency SLOs (<=120ms p95 for 512 tokens), data residency and KMS/SAML for enterprise later. They want a short benchmark + trial and security docs.

Topics: quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated, VPC/KMS, SOC2, rollout strategy

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on your account. Priya, do you want to intro?
[00:12] Priya Shah: Yep hi, I'm Priya, SE. I'll do the technical walkthrough and help scope the bench. Quick q before we start, Sam, can you remind us what you're trying to validate with Redwood?
[00:22] Sam Lee: Sure. We're building a real-time recommender for our mobile app, so latency is big. We also want a fast path for engineers to try things out — the PLG quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token, that sort of thing.
[00:34] Jordan Kim: And from infra side, we have VPC-only rules for prod but for evaluation we can use hosted if it's isolated. Also KMS for any customer PII.
[00:45] Alex Morgan: Great. On the PLG side we have a self-serve Redwood API, quickstart with SDKs, and free credits for new accounts. Typical time-to-first-token is under 10 minutes for a developer following the quickstart. Depends on whether you hit streaming or call patterns but 5–15 minutes is normal.
[01:05] Sam Lee: 5–15 minutes is pretty good. Is that for hosted only? What about Dedicated/Private spin up time?
[01:12] Priya Shah: Good question — hosted is immediate. Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool — provisioning usually takes days to weeks depending on capacity and contract. Private (VPC/on-prem) involves more setup and can take a few weeks, especially if you need HSM/KMS and audit log integrations.
[01:30] Jordan Kim: So for our evaluation we'll probably start hosted. We just need assurances about data handling and that logs don't persist. Do you have SOC 2 and data retention controls?
[01:40] Alex Morgan: Yes, we have SOC 2 and ISO in our enterprise pack, and we offer configurable retention and audit logs. For quickstarts we redact PII by default but you can opt into no-retain in the trial. I'll send the security pack after this call.
[01:55] Sam Lee: Awesome. On the model side: what models are in the catalog, and do you do quantization / lower-cost variants?
[02:05] Priya Shah: We curate open models and show performance profiles. We recommend quantized variants for lower-cost runs — Redwood Optimize gives suggestions for quantization and batching. For the quickstart you'll see the default model profile; for dedicated we can recommend specific quantization/kernel combos to meet your latency SLO.
[02:25] Alex Morgan: Also worth noting: smart routing and automatic fallbacks — if you need lower latency we can route to a higher-tier region or dedicated pool; if cost is priority we fall back to a cheaper quantized variant.
[02:38] Jordan Kim: For latency SLOs, Sam mentioned 120ms p95 at 512 tokens, that's tough. What hardware and throughput options should we consider?
[02:48] Priya Shah: For that SLO I'd recommend dedicated A10x or H100 depending on concurrency. We can run a short benchmark on your prompt set to recommend which instance type hits the SLO without overprovisioning.
[03:05] Sam Lee: Nice. What's the benchmark look like? How long, what do you need from our side?
[03:12] Priya Shah: Usually 1 hour of synthetic load with your prompt set and concurrency targets. We'll ask you to share 50–100 representative prompts, expected concurrency, and SLOs. We'll run it in our dedicated test environment (or hosted if you prefer) and return latency/cost tradeoffs.
[03:30] Alex Morgan: For PLG quickstarts we also provide a sandbox account with free credits — typically 30k tokens, sometimes more depending on the use case. That should be enough to exercise streaming and embedding flows.
[03:44] Sam Lee: That should be fine. How do devs authenticate? SSO? API keys?
[03:50] Alex Morgan: For dev accounts it's API keys and optional OAuth flow. For enterprise you can enable SAML/SSO and RBAC. We integrate with common IdPs and you can manage roles via Console.
[04:02] Jordan Kim: And for KMS — if we want to manage keys on-prem, is that supported?
[04:06] Priya Shah: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For hosted we can also integrate with customer KMS in many cases; we'll need to scope network connectivity and key policy.
[04:18] Sam Lee: Good. On pricing — for evaluation we're fine with credits, but long-term we'd consider reserved capacity for cost predictability. What's the threshold for dedicated?
[04:27] Alex Morgan: Dedicated is typically reserved monthly contracts, starts at a predictable throughput tier. We can share a pricing matrix — I'll include it in the follow-up. For PLG-to-Dedicated conversion we often do a pilot that demonstrates cost/perf and then convert under an enterprise deal.
[04:42] Priya Shah: Also highlight Redwood Optimize recommendations — batching and prefix caching can drop unit costs significantly. We can show estimated cost savings based on your token distribution.
[04:55] Sam Lee: That caching bit is interesting. We have a lot of repeated prefixes in recommendation prompts, so KV cache would help.
[05:02] Priya Shah: Exactly — KV caching and automatic prefix cache reduce per-token GPU work. We'll capture your prefix patterns in the bench.
[05:12] Alex Morgan: Any blockers for you to start the quickstart today? We can create the sandbox account and send the guide.
[05:19] Sam Lee: No blockers. I'd like Jordan to confirm infra policy for the sandbox though — we may need it whitelisted or a temporary IP allowlist.
[05:27] Jordan Kim: Yeah we'll need an allowlist. Also please confirm retention off for trial.
[05:32] Alex Morgan: We can do an allowlist and set retention to no-retain for the trial. I'll send details after.
[05:38] Sam Lee: Great. A few other questions: any limits on streaming sessions / webhooks? How does fallback work on errors?
[05:46] Priya Shah: Streaming is supported and standard limits apply in trial but are usually generous. For error fallback we have retry policies and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant; you can configure route policies in Console for production.
[06:00] Jordan Kim: For observability — do you provide token-level cost breakdowns and traces?
[06:05] Alex Morgan: Yes, Console gives per-route and per-model token-level cost, tracing hooks, and error analysis. You can export logs to your SIEM via S3 or streaming.
[06:15] Sam Lee: Good. Any legal/contractual red flags? We have some regulated customers.
[06:19] Alex Morgan: For regulated customers we offer Private deployments and on-prem packages; we also offer enterprise compliance add-ons (longer retention of audit logs, SOC2 documentation, dedicated support).
[06:30] Sam Lee: What's a typical timeline if we decide to go Private later?
[06:34] Priya Shah: Private can take several weeks to a couple months depending on infra readiness, network, HSM provisioning, and procurement. We'll help with the architecture plan.
[06:45] Jordan Kim: Ok. One last technical: do you support self-hosted vector DB or integrations for embeddings?
[06:52] Priya Shah: We integrate with common vector DBs; embeddings are available from the API. For private deployments we can enable direct network connections to your vector DB, or you can use our managed embedding store.
[07:05] Sam Lee: Solid. Let's recap next steps.
[07:08] Alex Morgan: Recap: I'll send trial account + quickstart guide and security pack; Priya will schedule a 1-hr benchmark and work with Jordan on prompts/allowlist; Sam will share prompt set and SLOs.
[07:21] Sam Lee: Yep sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:25] Jordan Kim: Thanks.
[07:27] Priya Shah: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites.

(End of transcript — occasional transcription errors may be present. Some product names transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood Privatee" in places.)
